draft.title: Area of rectangles and triangles
card: Rectangle
Area is the space inside a shape. For a rectangle, \(\text{area} = \text{length} \times \text{width}\). It is measured in square units, such as cm squared.
Triangle
A triangle's area is half the base times the perpendicular height. The perpendicular height meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted side.
Why half
Two copies of a triangle can make a rectangle with the same base and height. So the triangle is half of that rectangle.
Example
A triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Multiply \(10 \times 6 = 60\), then halve it to get 30 square centimetres.
draft.remember: Triangle area is half of base times perpendicular height. Do not forget the half.

a.q: A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its area?
a.why: Area is length times width, so \(9 \times 4 = 36\) square centimetres. Adding the sides to get 13 is a mistake, because adding does not measure the space inside the shape.

b.q: A triangle has a base of 12 cm, a perpendicular height of 5 cm and a slanted side of 13 cm. What is its area?
b.why: Area is half the base times the perpendicular height: \(\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5 = 30\). Using the slanted side of 13 cm gives 78, but the slanted side is not the perpendicular height.
b.clue: Use the height that meets the base at a right angle.

wants.brief: A triangle with a horizontal base labelled base, a dashed vertical line from the top corner to the base labelled perpendicular height with a small right-angle mark, and one slanted side labelled slanted side.
wants.why: It shows which length is the perpendicular height and which is not.

problems.detail: The 'Why half' line says two copies of a triangle make a rectangle with the same base and height. This is only true for right-angled triangles. Two copies of a general triangle make a parallelogram. A safer version: the triangle fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height and fills exactly half of it.

proposal.title: Area of rectangles and triangles
card: Rectangle
Area is the space inside a shape. For a rectangle, area \(=\) length \(\times\) width. It is measured in square units, such as square centimetres (\(\text{cm}^{2}\)).
Triangle
A triangle's area is half the base times the perpendicular height. The perpendicular height meets the base at a right angle. It is not the slanted side.
Why half
When the top corner sits above the base, the triangle fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. It fills exactly half of that rectangle.
Example
A triangle has base 10 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm. Multiply \(10 \times 6 = 60\), then halve it to get 30 square centimetres.
